privacy: This template holds counts only: one row per cancer group per quarter.
Do not add names, personal identity codes, dates of birth, addresses, individual dates or any free text about a patient.

Before you share a filled sheet outside your organisation, replace every count from 1 to 4 with "<5" (a common small-number rule; follow your own organisation's data protection guidance where it is stricter).
cancer_groups: All cancers (total of the rows above)

sections.title: How each new cancer was first found
sections.why: Finland does not publish how cancers are first found. A high share found at emergency visits points to people not getting through, or not being recognised, earlier.

abroad.text: England's National Disease Registration Service publishes, by area, the share of cancers first diagnosed after an emergency presentation.

data_gap.missing: How each cancer was first found (GP referral, screening or emergency visit), by area

measure.title: Create the legal basis for a national cancer care quality register at THL's Finnish Cancer Registry
measure.indicator: The register's data, including stage at diagnosis, allow quality and effectiveness to be assessed and compared reliably (coverage 90%).

fields.count: Number of new cancer diagnoses made in the quarter.

fields.header: …first found after a GP or primary-care referral
fields.count: Of A1: those whose route began with a referral from a GP or other primary-care professional.
Of A1: those found through a national screening programme (breast, cervical, bowel).
Of A1: those whose route began with an emergency department visit or an emergency admission.
Of A1: all others. A2 + A3 + A4 + A5 = A1.

sections.title: Suspected cancer at the GP
sections.why: The GP wait figure (Sotkanet 6411) covers every non-urgent visit. Marking the contacts where cancer is suspected lets the county see whether those people wait less.

basis.text: Uses the same 7-day line as Sotkanet 6411 (visits more than 7 days after the need was assessed).

data_gap.missing: How long people with possible cancer symptoms wait for a GP appointment

fields.count: Number of primary-care contacts in the quarter where a professional marked cancer as suspected.
Of B1: those seen by a doctor within 7 days of the contact.

sections.title: From referral to the first specialist visit
sections.why: Sotkanet 13 shows how fast the hospital processes a referral, not when the person is seen. THL's guide for monitoring access to cancer care names this interval: from the day the referral arrives to the first doctor visit.

basis.text: THL Ohjaus 21/2016: time points are the referral's arrival in specialist care and the first doctor visit after it (or a care call that replaces it).

data_gap.missing: Days from GP referral to diagnosis, by area

measure.title: Define national quality and effectiveness targets and the indicators for following the care pathways
measure.indicator: National, uniform targets and the key effectiveness indicators are defined for the agreed cancers.

fields.header: First specialist visit within 14 days of referral
fields.count: Of the suspected-cancer referrals that had their first specialist doctor visit in this quarter: those seen within 0–14 days of the referral arriving.
As C1, seen 15–28 days after the referral arrived.
As C1, seen more than 28 days after the referral arrived.

sections.title: From referral to diagnosis
sections.why: Days to diagnosis is not published in Finland. Denmark measured this interval before and after its fast-track pathways; England publishes a 28-day standard for being told the diagnosis.

abroad.text: NHS England publishes every month, by area and hospital, the share of people referred with suspected cancer who are told their diagnosis within 28 days. Denmark's study measured the same interval before and after fast-track pathways.

data_gap.missing: Days from GP referral to diagnosis, by area

measure.title: Define national quality and effectiveness targets and the indicators for following the care pathways
measure.indicator: National, uniform targets and the key effectiveness indicators are defined for the agreed cancers.

fields.count: Of the cancers diagnosed this quarter that began with a referral: those diagnosed 0–28 days after the referral arrived.
As D1, diagnosed 29–42 days after the referral arrived.
As D1, diagnosed more than 42 days after the referral arrived.

sections.title: From referral to the first cancer treatment
sections.why: This is the strategy's Goal 3 measure: patients reach care within the target times. Nothing is published by area yet; counting it now means the figure exists when the national target times are set.

basis.text: THL Ohjaus 21/2016 follows the time from the referral's arrival to the first cancer treatment, and quotes the national working group's maximum for suspected cancer: 6 weeks.

abroad.text: NHS England publishes every month, by area and hospital, the share of people starting cancer treatment within 62 days of an urgent referral.

data_gap.missing: Share of patients who start treatment within the target time, by area

measure.title: Write national care pathway descriptions for each cancer, with regional pathways based on them and a way to maintain and manage them
measure.indicator: Patients get to care within the target times.

fields.header: First treatment within 6 weeks of referral
fields.count: Of the patients whose first cancer treatment started this quarter: those who started within 42 days of the referral arriving.
As E1, started more than 42 days after the referral arrived.

sections.title: Stage at diagnosis (ask the Cancer Registry)
sections.why: Stage by area is not published. The roadmap's target is that at least 70% of cancers are found at stages I–II by 2035. The county does not record this itself: it asks the Finnish Cancer Registry and enters the counts here.

measure.title: Create the legal basis for a national cancer care quality register at THL's Finnish Cancer Registry
measure.indicator: The register's data, including stage at diagnosis, allow quality and effectiveness to be assessed and compared reliably (coverage 90%).

fields.header: Stage I–II at diagnosis (from the Cancer Registry)
fields.count: Of A1, from the Finnish Cancer Registry when available: cancers at stage I or II.
As F1, stage III or IV.
As F1, stage not recorded or not applicable.

indicators.name: Share of new cancers first found at an emergency visit
indicators.compare_with: England publishes this by area (National Disease Registration Service).

indicators.name: Share of new cancers found through screening
indicators.compare_with: Your own area over time; screening attendance itself is in Sotkanet 3621, 6103 and 3620.

indicators.name: Share of suspected-cancer GP contacts seen by a doctor within 7 days
indicators.compare_with: The all-visit figure, Sotkanet 6411 (which counts the visits that took longer than 7 days).

indicators.name: Share of first specialist visits within 14 days of the referral
indicators.compare_with: Your own area over time. 14 days is a reporting band, not a Finnish target.

indicators.name: Share diagnosed within 28 days of the referral
indicators.compare_with: England's 28-day standard for being told the diagnosis (NHS England, monthly by area).

indicators.name: Share starting cancer treatment within 6 weeks of the referral
indicators.compare_with: Goal 3's measure, 'patients reach care within the target times'. Until FICAN sets the target times, 6 weeks is the maximum the national working group set for suspected cancer (quoted in THL Ohjaus 21/2016).

indicators.name: Share of cancers found at stage I–II
indicators.formula: F1 ÷ (F1 + F2) × 100 (cancers with stage not known left out; report how many)
indicators.compare_with: The roadmap's target: at least 70% at stages I–II by 2035.
